name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_P_BLOCK_ELEMENTS_MATCH_Q01 - Important minerals of boron and aluminium with formulae

questiontext.text:
Match List-I (Minerals) with List-II (Chemical Formulae):

List-I (Mineral)List-II (Formula)
(a) Borax(i) \(\mathrm{Al_2O_3\cdot 2H_2O}\)
(b) Kernite(ii) \(\mathrm{Na_2B_4O_7\cdot 10H_2O}\)
(c) Bauxite(iii) \(\mathrm{Na_3AlF_6}\)
(d) Cryolite(iv) \(\mathrm{Na_2B_4O_7\cdot 4H_2O}\)

Choose the correct match from the options given below.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Boron and aluminium occur naturally in the Earth's crust primarily as hydrated borates, hydrated oxides, and complex fluorides.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Mineral
- Borax is hydrated sodium tetraborate decahydrate with formula \(\mathrm{Na_2B_4O_7\cdot 10H_2O}\) (more accurately \(\mathrm{Na_2[B_4O_5(OH)_4]\cdot 8H_2O}\)).
- Kernite is a lower hydrate of sodium tetraborate with formula \(\mathrm{Na_2B_4O_7\cdot 4H_2O}\).
- Bauxite is the principal ore of aluminium, consisting of hydrated aluminium oxide with formula \(\mathrm{Al_2O_3\cdot 2H_2O}\).
- Cryolite is sodium hexafluoroaluminate(III) with formula \(\mathrm{Na_3AlF_6}\).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct conceptual pairing is: Borax \(\rightarrow \mathrm{Na_2B_4O_7\cdot 10H_2O}\), Kernite \(\rightarrow \mathrm{Na_2B_4O_7\cdot 4H_2O}\), Bauxite \(\rightarrow \mathrm{Al_2O_3\cdot 2H_2O}\), and Cryolite \(\rightarrow \mathrm{Na_3AlF_6}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_P_BLOCK_ELEMENTS_MATCH_Q02 - Common names and chemical formulae of p-block compounds

questiontext.text:
Match List-I (Common Name / Mineral) with List-II (Chemical Formula / Identity):

List-IList-II
(a) Cassiterite(i) Solid \(\mathrm{CO_2}\)
(b) Galena(ii) \(\mathrm{B_3N_3H_6}\)
(c) Dry ice(iii) \(\mathrm{SnO_2}\)
(d) Inorganic benzene(iv) \(\mathrm{PbS}\)

Choose the correct match from the options given below.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Several p-block ores and compounds are widely known by traditional or structural names based on their composition or similarity to organic rings.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Entry
- Cassiterite is the main ore of tin, consisting of tin(IV) oxide, \(\mathrm{SnO_2}\).
- Galena is the principal ore of lead, consisting of lead(II) sulphide, \(\mathrm{PbS}\).
- Dry ice is solid carbon dioxide, \(\mathrm{CO_2}\), obtained by rapid expansion of liquefied \(\mathrm{CO_2}\).
- Inorganic benzene is borazine, \(\mathrm{B_3N_3H_6}\), named for its six-membered ring structure with alternating \(\mathrm{BH}\) and \(\mathrm{NH}\) groups.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct conceptual pairing is: Cassiterite \(\rightarrow \mathrm{SnO_2}\), Galena \(\rightarrow \mathrm{PbS}\), Dry ice \(\rightarrow\) Solid \(\mathrm{CO_2}\), and Inorganic benzene \(\rightarrow \mathrm{B_3N_3H_6}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_P_BLOCK_ELEMENTS_MATCH_Q03 - Practical applications of boron and carbon materials

questiontext.text:
Match List-I (Application) with List-II (Substance):

List-I (Application)List-II (Substance)
(a) Making bullet-proof vests(i) Graphite
(b) Control rods in nuclear reactors(ii) Boron fibres
(c) Mild antiseptic(iii) Metal borides (\({}^{10}\mathrm{B}\))
(d) Dry lubricant at high temperature(iv) Aqueous orthoboric acid

Choose the correct match from the options given below.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The industrial and everyday uses of boron, carbon, and their compounds stem directly from their mechanical, nuclear, chemical, and structural properties.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Application
- Boron fibres are extremely hard and lightweight, making them suitable for bullet-proof vests and light composite materials for aircraft.
- The \({}^{10}\mathrm{B}\) isotope has a high neutron-absorption cross-section, so metal borides are used in the nuclear industry as protective shields and control rods.
- A dilute aqueous solution of orthoboric acid (\(\mathrm{H_3BO_3}\)) is used as a mild antiseptic.
- Graphite cleaves easily between its van der Waals-bonded layers, making it soft and slippery, so it is used as a dry lubricant in high-temperature machines where oil cannot be used.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct conceptual matches are: bullet-proof vests \(\rightarrow\) Boron fibres, nuclear control rods \(\rightarrow\) Metal borides (\({}^{10}\mathrm{B}\)), mild antiseptic \(\rightarrow\) Aqueous orthoboric acid, and dry lubricant \(\rightarrow\) Graphite.

questiontext.text:
Match List-I (Group 13 Oxide) with List-II (Acid-Base Nature):

List-I (Oxide)List-II (Nature)
(a) \(\mathrm{B_2O_3}\)(i) Basic
(b) \(\mathrm{Al_2O_3}\)(ii) Acidic
(c) \(\mathrm{In_2O_3}\)(iii) Amphoteric
(d) \(\mathrm{Tl_2O_3}\)(iv) Basic

Note: Match \(\mathrm{Al_2O_3}\) to its specific behaviour and distinguish the acidic oxide from the basic oxides.

Choose the correct match from the options given below.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Across Group \(13\), metallic character increases down the group from boron (non-metal) to aluminium and gallium (borderline/amphoteric) to indium and thallium (metals). Consequently, the nature of their trioxides (\(\mathrm{E_2O_3}\)) shifts from acidic to amphoteric to basic.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Oxide
- Boron trioxide (\(\mathrm{B_2O_3}\)) is acidic and reacts with basic metallic oxides to form metal borates.
- Aluminium oxide (\(\mathrm{Al_2O_3}\)) (along with \(\mathrm{Ga_2O_3}\)) is amphoteric, reacting with both acids and alkalies.
- Indium oxide (\(\mathrm{In_2O_3}\)) and thallium oxide (\(\mathrm{Tl_2O_3}\)) are basic in nature.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct conceptual matching pairs \(\mathrm{B_2O_3}\) with acidic, \(\mathrm{Al_2O_3}\) with amphoteric, and both \(\mathrm{In_2O_3}\) and \(\mathrm{Tl_2O_3}\) with basic.

questiontext.text:
Match List-I (Group 14 Oxide) with List-II (Nature):

List-I (Oxide)List-II (Nature)
(a) \(\mathrm{CO}\)(i) Distinctly acidic
(b) \(\mathrm{GeO}\)(ii) Neutral
(c) \(\mathrm{PbO_2}\)(iii) Acidic
(d) \(\mathrm{SiO_2}\)(iv) Amphoteric

Choose the correct match from the options given below.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Group \(14\) elements form monoxides (\(\mathrm{MO}\)) and dioxides (\(\mathrm{MO_2}\)). Oxides in higher oxidation states are generally more acidic than those in lower oxidation states, and metallic character increases down the group.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Oxide
- Carbon monoxide (\(\mathrm{CO}\)) is a neutral oxide.
- Germanium monoxide (\(\mathrm{GeO}\)) is distinctly acidic.
- Lead dioxide (\(\mathrm{PbO_2}\)) (along with \(\mathrm{SnO_2}\), \(\mathrm{SnO}\), and \(\mathrm{PbO}\)) is amphoteric.
- Silicon dioxide (\(\mathrm{SiO_2}\)) (along with \(\mathrm{CO_2}\) and \(\mathrm{GeO_2}\)) is acidic, reacting with strong bases such as \(\mathrm{NaOH}\) to form silicates.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct conceptual pairing is: \(\mathrm{CO} \rightarrow\) Neutral, \(\mathrm{GeO} \rightarrow\) Distinctly acidic, \(\mathrm{PbO_2} \rightarrow\) Amphoteric, and \(\mathrm{SiO_2} \rightarrow\) Acidic.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_P_BLOCK_ELEMENTS_MATCH_Q06 - Hybridisation of central atom in p-block species

questiontext.text:
Match List-I (Species) with List-II (Hybridisation of Central Atom):

List-I (Species)List-II (Hybridisation)
(a) \(\mathrm{BF_3}\)(i) \(sp\)
(b) \([\mathrm{BH_4}]^-\)(ii) \(sp^3d^2\)
(c) \([\mathrm{Al(H_2O)_6}]^{3+}\)(iii) \(sp^2\)
(d) \(\mathrm{CO_2}\)(iv) \(sp^3\)

Choose the correct match from the options given below.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The hybridisation of a central atom is determined by the number of \(\sigma\)-bonds plus lone pairs (steric number) around it: \(2 \rightarrow sp\), \(3 \rightarrow sp^2\), \(4 \rightarrow sp^3\), \(6 \rightarrow sp^3d^2\).

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Species
- In \(\mathrm{BF_3}\), boron forms \(3\) \(\sigma\)-bonds with \(0\) lone pairs, so it is \(sp^2\) hybridised (trigonal planar).
- In \([\mathrm{BH_4}]^-\), boron forms \(4\) \(\sigma\)-bonds with \(0\) lone pairs, so it is \(sp^3\) hybridised (tetrahedral).
- In \([\mathrm{Al(H_2O)_6}]^{3+}\), aluminium uses its \(3s\), \(3p\), and \(3d\) orbitals to coordinate six water molecules, giving \(sp^3d^2\) hybridisation (octahedral).
- In \(\mathrm{CO_2}\), carbon forms \(2\) \(\sigma\)-bonds and \(2\) \(\pi\)-bonds with \(0\) lone pairs, so it is \(sp\) hybridised (linear).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct conceptual pairing is: \(\mathrm{BF_3} \rightarrow sp^2\), \([\mathrm{BH_4}]^- \rightarrow sp^3\), \([\mathrm{Al(H_2O)_6}]^{3+} \rightarrow sp^3d^2\), and \(\mathrm{CO_2} \rightarrow sp\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_P_BLOCK_ELEMENTS_MATCH_Q07 - Synthesis and composition of industrial carbon oxides

questiontext.text:
Match List-I (Process / Fuel Gas) with List-II (Product / Composition):

List-IList-II
(a) Water gas (synthesis gas)(i) Pure \(\mathrm{CO}\)
(b) Producer gas(ii) \(\mathrm{CO_2}\)
(c) Dehydration of \(\mathrm{HCOOH}\) with conc. \(\mathrm{H_2SO_4}\) at \(373\text{ K}\)(iii) \(\mathrm{CO + N_2}\)
(d) Action of dilute \(\mathrm{HCl}\) on \(\mathrm{CaCO_3}\)(iv) \(\mathrm{CO + H_2}\)

Choose the correct match from the options given below.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Carbon monoxide and carbon dioxide are prepared by distinct laboratory and industrial methods, and \(\mathrm{CO}\) forms important gaseous fuel mixtures with \(\mathrm{H_2}\) or \(\mathrm{N_2}\).

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Process
- Passing steam over hot coke (\(473\text{–}1273\text{ K}\)) yields water gas (synthesis gas), a mixture of \(\mathrm{CO}\) and \(\mathrm{H_2}\).
- Passing air over hot coke (\(1273\text{ K}\)) yields producer gas, a mixture of \(\mathrm{CO}\) and \(\mathrm{N_2}\).
- On a small scale, pure \(\mathrm{CO}\) is prepared by dehydrating formic acid (\(\mathrm{HCOOH}\)) with concentrated \(\mathrm{H_2SO_4}\) at \(373\text{ K}\).
- In the laboratory, \(\mathrm{CO_2}\) is conveniently prepared by treating calcium carbonate (\(\mathrm{CaCO_3}\)) with dilute \(\mathrm{HCl}\).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct conceptual pairing is: Water gas \(\rightarrow \mathrm{CO + H_2}\), Producer gas \(\rightarrow \mathrm{CO + N_2}\), Dehydration of \(\mathrm{HCOOH} \rightarrow\) Pure \(\mathrm{CO}\), and \(\mathrm{CaCO_3 + dil.\ HCl} \rightarrow \mathrm{CO_2}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_P_BLOCK_ELEMENTS_MATCH_Q08 - Thermal and redox reactions of boron compounds

questiontext.text:
Match List-I (Reaction) with List-II (Major Boron-Containing Product):

List-I (Reaction)List-II (Product)
(a) Strong heating of borax (\(\mathrm{Na_2B_4O_7\cdot 10H_2O}\))(i) \(\mathrm{B_2H_6}\)
(b) Heating \(\mathrm{H_3BO_3}\) above \(370\text{ K}\)(ii) \(\mathrm{B_3N_3H_6}\)
(c) Heating \(\mathrm{B_2H_6\cdot 2NH_3}\)(iii) \(\mathrm{HBO_2}\)
(d) Oxidation of \(\mathrm{NaBH_4}\) with \(\mathrm{I_2}\)(iv) \(\mathrm{NaBO_2 + B_2O_3}\)

Choose the correct match from the options given below.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Borax, orthoboric acid, and diborane undergo characteristic thermal dehydration, decomposition, and redox reactions to yield metaborates, metaboric acid, borazine, and boranes.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Reaction
- On strong heating, borax first loses water of crystallisation and then melts to form a transparent glassy bead containing sodium metaborate and boric anhydride (\(\mathrm{2NaBO_2 + B_2O_3}\)).
- On heating orthoboric acid (\(\mathrm{H_3BO_3}\)) above \(370\text{ K}\), it dehydrates to metaboric acid (\(\mathrm{HBO_2}\)).
- Heating the diborane-ammonia adduct \(\mathrm{B_2H_6\cdot 2NH_3}\) (formulated as \([\mathrm{BH_2(NH_3)_2}]^+[\mathrm{BH_4}]^-\)) gives borazine (\(\mathrm{B_3N_3H_6}\)) and \(\mathrm{H_2}\).
- A convenient laboratory preparation of diborane (\(\mathrm{B_2H_6}\)) involves the oxidation of sodium borohydride (\(\mathrm{NaBH_4}\)) with iodine (\(\mathrm{I_2}\)): \(2\mathrm{NaBH_4} + \mathrm{I_2} \rightarrow \mathrm{B_2H_6} + 2\mathrm{NaI} + \mathrm{H_2}\).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct conceptual pairing is: strong heating of borax \(\rightarrow \mathrm{NaBO_2 + B_2O_3}\), heating \(\mathrm{H_3BO_3}\) above \(370\text{ K} \rightarrow \mathrm{HBO_2}\), heating \(\mathrm{B_2H_6\cdot 2NH_3} \rightarrow \mathrm{B_3N_3H_6}\), and oxidation of \(\mathrm{NaBH_4}\) with \(\mathrm{I_2} \rightarrow \mathrm{B_2H_6}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_P_BLOCK_ELEMENTS_MATCH_Q09 - Industrial uses of silica forms and zeolites

questiontext.text:
Match List-I (Silica / Aluminosilicate Material) with List-II (Primary Use):

List-I (Material)List-II (Use)
(a) Quartz(i) Catalyst to convert alcohols directly into gasoline
(b) Silica gel(ii) Filtration plants
(c) Kieselguhr(iii) Piezoelectric material in accurate clocks
(d) ZSM-5(iv) Drying agent and chromatographic support

Choose the correct match from the options given below.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Different crystalline, amorphous, and aluminosilicate forms of silicon dioxide possess distinct physical and catalytic properties suited to specific technologies.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Material
- Quartz is extensively used as a piezoelectric material in accurate clocks, modern radio/TV broadcasting, and mobile communications.
- Silica gel is widely used as a drying agent and as a support for chromatographic materials and catalysts.
- Kieselguhr, an amorphous form of silica, is used in filtration plants.
- ZSM-5 is a zeolite catalyst used in petrochemical industries to convert alcohols directly into gasoline.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct conceptual pairing is: Quartz \(\rightarrow\) Piezoelectric material, Silica gel \(\rightarrow\) Drying agent and chromatographic support, Kieselguhr \(\rightarrow\) Filtration plants, and ZSM-5 \(\rightarrow\) Catalyst for converting alcohols directly into gasoline.

questiontext.text:
Match List-I (Group 13 Element) with List-II (Characteristic Property):

List-I (Element)List-II (Property)
(a) Boron(i) Most abundant metal in Earth's crust (\(8.3\%\))
(b) Aluminium(ii) Unusually low melting point (\(303\text{ K}\)) and high boiling point (\(2676\text{ K}\))
(c) Gallium(iii) Predominant \(+1\) oxidation state due to inert pair effect
(d) Thallium(iv) Extremely hard black solid with highest melting point in Group 13

Choose the correct match from the options given below.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Group \(13\) elements show marked variations in abundance, melting points, and oxidation-state stabilities due to lattice structures and inner-core electronic effects.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Element
- Boron is a non-metallic, extremely hard black solid with a very strong crystalline lattice, giving it an unusually high melting point (\(2453\text{ K}\)), the highest in Group \(13\).
- Aluminium is the most abundant metal and third most abundant element in the Earth's crust (\(8.3\%\) by mass).
- Gallium has an unusually low melting point (\(303\text{ K}\), allowing it to exist as a liquid in summer) and a high boiling point (\(2676\text{ K}\)), making it useful for measuring high temperatures.
- Thallium predominantly exhibits the \(+1\) oxidation state because poor shielding by \(4f\) and \(5d\) electrons holds its \(6s^2\) pair tightly (inert pair effect).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct conceptual pairing is: Boron \(\rightarrow\) Extremely hard black solid with highest melting point, Aluminium \(\rightarrow\) Most abundant metal in Earth's crust, Gallium \(\rightarrow\) Low melting point (\(303\text{ K}\)) and high boiling point (\(2676\text{ K}\)), and Thallium \(\rightarrow\) Predominant \(+1\) oxidation state.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_P_BLOCK_ELEMENTS_MATCH_Q11 - Preparation and uses of elemental forms of carbon

questiontext.text:
Match List-I (Form of Carbon) with List-II (Preparation / Use):

List-I (Form of Carbon)List-II (Preparation / Use)
(a) Fullerenes(i) Obtained by burning hydrocarbons in limited air; used in black ink
(b) Carbon black(ii) Obtained by heating coal at high temperature in absence of air; reducing agent in metallurgy
(c) Coke(iii) Made by heating graphite in an electric arc in inert gas
(d) Activated charcoal(iv) Highly porous; used in adsorbing poisonous gases and water filtration

Choose the correct match from the options given below.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Elemental carbon exists as pure crystalline/molecular allotropes (diamond, graphite, fullerenes) as well as impure amorphous forms (carbon black, coke, charcoal) obtained by controlled pyrolysis or incomplete combustion.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Form
- Fullerenes are prepared by heating graphite in an electric arc in the presence of inert gases such as helium or argon.
- Carbon black is obtained by burning hydrocarbons in a limited supply of air and is used as a black pigment in ink and filler in automobile tyres.
- Coke is obtained by heating coal at high temperatures in the absence of air and is used as a fuel and reducing agent in metallurgy.
- Activated charcoal is highly porous and used to adsorb poisonous gases, remove organic contaminants in water filters, and control odour.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct conceptual pairing is: Fullerenes \(\rightarrow\) electric arc heating of graphite, Carbon black \(\rightarrow\) incomplete combustion of hydrocarbons, Coke \(\rightarrow\) pyrolysis of coal, and Activated charcoal \(\rightarrow\) adsorption of poisonous gases and water filtration.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_P_BLOCK_ELEMENTS_MATCH_Q12 - Redox and coordination behaviour of Group 14 species

questiontext.text:
Match List-I (Group 14 Species) with List-II (Characteristic Chemical Behaviour):

List-I (Species)List-II (Behaviour)
(a) \(\mathrm{Sn^{2+}}\)(i) Strong oxidising agent
(b) \(\mathrm{Pb^{4+}}\)(ii) Electron-precise, not hydrolysed by water
(c) \(\mathrm{CCl_4}\)(iii) \(sp^3d^2\) hybridised octahedral complex
(d) \([\mathrm{GeCl_6}]^{2-}\)(iv) Reducing agent

Choose the correct match from the options given below.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
In Group \(14\), the stability of the \(+2\) oxidation state relative to \(+4\) increases down the group (\(\mathrm{Ge} < \mathrm{Sn} < \mathrm{Pb}\)) due to the inert pair effect, while the availability of \(d\)-orbitals in heavier elements enables complexation and hydrolysis.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Species
- Tin in the \(+2\) state (\(\mathrm{Sn^{2+}}\)) tends to get oxidised to the more stable \(+4\) state, so \(\mathrm{Sn^{2+}}\) acts as a reducing agent.
- Lead in the \(+4\) state (\(\mathrm{Pb^{4+}}\)) readily accepts two electrons to form the much more stable \(+2\) state, so \(\mathrm{Pb^{4+}}\) is a strong oxidising agent.
- Carbon tetrachloride (\(\mathrm{CCl_4}\)) is an electron-precise molecule (\(8\) electrons around carbon) and lacks \(d\)-orbitals, so it is not hydrolysed by water.
- Hexachlorogermanate(IV) (\([\mathrm{GeCl_6}]^{2-}\)) is formed by germanium expanding its coordination number to \(6\) using vacant \(d\)-orbitals, resulting in \(sp^3d^2\) hybridisation and octahedral geometry.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct conceptual pairing is: \(\mathrm{Sn^{2+}} \rightarrow\) Reducing agent, \(\mathrm{Pb^{4+}} \rightarrow\) Strong oxidising agent, \(\mathrm{CCl_4} \rightarrow\) Electron-precise and not hydrolysed by water, and \([\mathrm{GeCl_6}]^{2-} \rightarrow sp^3d^2\) hybridised octahedral complex.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_P_BLOCK_ELEMENTS_MATCH_Q13 - Bond enthalpies and bond lengths in Group 14 and carbon allotropes

questiontext.text:
Match List-I (Bond / Structural Parameter) with List-II (Experimental Value):

List-IList-II
(a) \(\mathrm{C-C}\) bond enthalpy(i) \(141.5\text{ pm}\)
(b) \(\mathrm{Si-Si}\) bond enthalpy(ii) \(348\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}\)
(c) \(\mathrm{C-C}\) bond length in diamond(iii) \(297\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}\)
(d) \(\mathrm{C-C}\) bond length within a graphite layer(iv) \(154\text{ pm}\)

Choose the correct match from the options given below.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Catenation tendency in Group \(14\) decreases down the group as atomic size increases and \(\mathrm{M-M}\) bond enthalpy decreases. In carbon allotropes, \(\mathrm{C-C}\) bond length decreases as bond order increases from \(1\) (\(sp^3\) in diamond) to \(1.33\text{–}1.5\) (\(sp^2\) with \(\pi\)-delocalisation in graphite).

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Parameter
- The \(\mathrm{C-C}\) single bond enthalpy is \(348\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}\), explaining carbon's strong catenation.
- The \(\mathrm{Si-Si}\) single bond enthalpy is \(297\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}\) (followed by \(\mathrm{Ge-Ge} = 260\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}\) and \(\mathrm{Sn-Sn} = 240\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}\)).
- In diamond, each \(sp^3\) carbon forms four single bonds with a \(\mathrm{C-C}\) bond length of \(154\text{ pm}\).
- Within a planar hexagonal layer of graphite, each \(sp^2\) carbon has partial double-bond character, giving a shorter \(\mathrm{C-C}\) bond length of \(141.5\text{ pm}\).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct conceptual pairing is: \(\mathrm{C-C}\) bond enthalpy \(\rightarrow 348\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}\), \(\mathrm{Si-Si}\) bond enthalpy \(\rightarrow 297\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}\), diamond \(\mathrm{C-C}\) bond length \(\rightarrow 154\text{ pm}\), and graphite in-layer \(\mathrm{C-C}\) bond length \(\rightarrow 141.5\text{ pm}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_P_BLOCK_ELEMENTS_MATCH_Q14 - Role of chlorosilanes and silica reactions in silicon chemistry

questiontext.text:
Match List-I (Starting Material / Reaction) with List-II (Product / Role):

List-IList-II
(a) \((\mathrm{CH_3})_2\mathrm{SiCl_2}\)(i) Chain-terminating blocker to control silicone chain length
(b) \((\mathrm{CH_3})_3\mathrm{SiCl}\)(ii) \(\mathrm{SiF_4 + 2H_2O}\)
(c) \(\mathrm{RSiCl_3}\)(iii) Hydrolysis and condensation yield straight-chain silicone polymer
(d) \(\mathrm{SiO_2 + 4HF}\)(iv) Hydrolysis and condensation yield cross-linked silicone polymer

Choose the correct match from the options given below.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The structure and dimensionality of silicone polymers depend on the number of hydrolysable \(\mathrm{Si-Cl}\) groups on the organochlorosilane precursor (\(\mathrm{R_nSiCl_{4-n}}\)).

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Entry
- Dimethyldichlorosilane, \((\mathrm{CH_3})_2\mathrm{SiCl_2}\), has two \(\mathrm{Cl}\) atoms; hydrolysis gives \((\mathrm{CH_3})_2\mathrm{Si(OH)_2}\), which undergoes condensation polymerisation at both ends to form a straight-chain silicone.
- Trimethylchlorosilane, \((\mathrm{CH_3})_3\mathrm{SiCl}\), has only one \(\mathrm{Cl}\) atom; hydrolysis gives \((\mathrm{CH_3})_3\mathrm{SiOH}\), which condenses at only one site and therefore blocks the chain ends to control polymer length.
- Alkyltrichlorosilane, \(\mathrm{RSiCl_3}\), has three \(\mathrm{Cl}\) atoms; hydrolysis gives \(\mathrm{RSi(OH)_3}\), which can condense in three directions to yield a cross-linked silicone polymer.
- Silicon dioxide reacts with hydrofluoric acid according to \(\mathrm{SiO_2 + 4HF \rightarrow SiF_4 + 2H_2O}\).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct conceptual pairing is: \((\mathrm{CH_3})_2\mathrm{SiCl_2} \rightarrow\) straight-chain silicone, \((\mathrm{CH_3})_3\mathrm{SiCl} \rightarrow\) chain-terminating blocker, \(\mathrm{RSiCl_3} \rightarrow\) cross-linked silicone, and \(\mathrm{SiO_2 + 4HF} \rightarrow \mathrm{SiF_4 + 2H_2O}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_P_BLOCK_ELEMENTS_MATCH_Q15 - Thermodynamic and electrode potential values in p-block

questiontext.text:
Match List-I (Thermodynamic / Electrode Potential Quantity) with List-II (Value):

List-I (Quantity)List-II (Value)
(a) \(E^\circ(\mathrm{Al^{3+}/Al})\)(i) \(+38.1\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}\)
(b) \(E^\circ(\mathrm{Tl^{3+}/Tl})\)(ii) \(+1.26\text{ V}\)
(c) \(\Delta_f H^\circ\) of diamond(iii) \(-1.66\text{ V}\)
(d) \(\Delta_f H^\circ\) of fullerene (\(\mathrm{C_{60}}\))(iv) \(+1.90\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}\)

Choose the correct match from the options given below.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Standard reduction potentials reflect the relative stability of \(+3\) ions in aqueous solution, whereas standard enthalpies of formation of carbon allotropes are measured relative to graphite (\(\Delta_f H^\circ = 0\)).

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Quantity
- Aluminium readily forms \(\mathrm{Al^{3+}(aq)}\) and is highly electropositive, with \(E^\circ(\mathrm{Al^{3+}/Al}) = -1.66\text{ V}\).
- \(\mathrm{Tl^{3+}}\) is unstable in solution and acts as a powerful oxidising agent, with \(E^\circ(\mathrm{Tl^{3+}/Tl}) = +1.26\text{ V}\).
- Graphite is the thermodynamically most stable allotrope of carbon (\(\Delta_f H^\circ = 0\)), while diamond is slightly less stable with \(\Delta_f H^\circ = +1.90\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}\).
- Fullerene (\(\mathrm{C_{60}}\)) has a strained cage structure and a higher standard enthalpy of formation, \(\Delta_f H^\circ = +38.1\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}\).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct conceptual pairing is: \(E^\circ(\mathrm{Al^{3+}/Al}) \rightarrow -1.66\text{ V}\), \(E^\circ(\mathrm{Tl^{3+}/Tl}) \rightarrow +1.26\text{ V}\), \(\Delta_f H^\circ(\text{diamond}) \rightarrow +1.90\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}\), and \(\Delta_f H^\circ(\mathrm{C_{60}}) \rightarrow +38.1\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_P_BLOCK_ELEMENTS_MATCH_Q16 - Chemical reactions of diborane with various reagents

questiontext.text:
Match List-I (Reactants with Diborane) with List-II (Products):

List-I (Reactants)List-II (Products)
(a) \(\mathrm{B_2H_6 + 6H_2O}\)(i) \(2\mathrm{Na^+[BH_4]^-}\)
(b) \(\mathrm{B_2H_6 + 2NMe_3}\)(ii) \(\mathrm{B_2O_3 + 3H_2O}\)
(c) \(\mathrm{B_2H_6 + 2NaH}\)(iii) \(2\mathrm{BH_3\cdot NMe_3}\)
(d) \(\mathrm{B_2H_6 + 3O_2}\)(iv) \(2\mathrm{B(OH)_3 + 6H_2}\)

Choose the correct match from the options given below.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Diborane (\(\mathrm{B_2H_6}\)) undergoes hydrolysis with water, symmetrical cleavage with Lewis bases, hydride transfer with metal hydrides, and highly exothermic combustion with dioxygen.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Reaction
- Hydrolysis of diborane with water yields orthoboric acid and dihydrogen gas: \(\mathrm{B_2H_6(g) + 6H_2O(l) \rightarrow 2B(OH)_3(aq) + 6H_2(g)}\).
- Cleavage of diborane with trimethylamine (\(\mathrm{NMe_3}\)) gives the borane adduct: \(\mathrm{B_2H_6 + 2NMe_3 \rightarrow 2BH_3\cdot NMe_3}\).
- Reaction of diborane with sodium hydride in diethyl ether yields sodium tetrahydridoborate (sodium borohydride): \(\mathrm{B_2H_6 + 2NaH \rightarrow 2Na^+[BH_4]^-}\).
- Combustion of diborane in oxygen releases an enormous amount of energy (\(\Delta_r H^\circ = -1976\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}\)): \(\mathrm{B_2H_6 + 3O_2 \rightarrow B_2O_3 + 3H_2O}\).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct conceptual pairing is: \(\mathrm{B_2H_6 + 6H_2O} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{B(OH)_3 + 6H_2}\), \(\mathrm{B_2H_6 + 2NMe_3} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{BH_3\cdot NMe_3}\), \(\mathrm{B_2H_6 + 2NaH} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{Na^+[BH_4]^-}\), and \(\mathrm{B_2H_6 + 3O_2} \rightarrow \mathrm{B_2O_3 + 3H_2O}\).
